entries.title: II Samuel 4:1
segments: A common method by which God overthrows nations and parties that oppose themselves to his righteous couse, is to take from them the wise and strong men to whom they trusted as leaders.

entries.title: II Samuel 4:4
segments:
The tidings came; of the death of Saul and Jonathan. 
 
Many are the dangers of life and limb to which little children are exposed, and the kindness of God in their preservation and comfort is constant and great.

entries.title: II Samuel 4:6
segments:
As though they would have fetched wheat; more literally, fetching wheat.  To conceal their guilty purpose they fetched wheat, as though this was their business. 
 
Rulers who depend for support only on soldiers, can never be safe; many who for a time fight against them and even take their life.

entries.title: II Samuel 4:7
segments: The plain; the Jordan valley, which lay between Mahanaim and Hebron.

entries.title: II Samuel 4:8
segments: Men often glory in iniquity, and speak of treason, bloodshed, and murder as if they were pleasing to God, and entitled the perpetrators to the gratitude of their fellow men.

entries.title: II Samuel 4:9
segments: Men who trust in God will not commit sin to accomplish his or their purposes; nor will they reward it or connive at it in others.

entries.title: II Samuel 4:11
segments: A righteous person; innocent as to his murderers, one who had done them no wrong.

entries.title: II Samuel 4:12
segments: All who expect in the end to be gainers by the commission of sin, will meet with sure and woeful disappointment.
